A.explanation: Both exponents negative would make $v$ decrease when $T$ increases, which contradicts the physics that higher tension gives higher wave speed.

B.explanation: This reverses the dependence, giving $v$ decreasing with $T$ and increasing with $\mu$, whereas a heavier wire at fixed tension carries slower waves.

C.explanation: With $p = 1/2$ and $q = -1/2$, the base units on both sides match $\text{m s}^{-1}$, giving $v = \sqrt{T/\mu}$.

D.explanation: Both exponents positive would make $v$ increase with mass per unit length $\mu$, but greater inertia at fixed tension must reduce the wave speed.

hints: Write the base units of each quantity: $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, tension $T$ as a force in $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, and $\mu$ as mass per length in $\text{kg m}^{-1}$.
Require homogeneity by equating powers of $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ on the two sides of $v = T^p \mu^q$.
Use the time powers first since only $T$ contains $\text{s}$ to find $p$, then use the mass powers $p+q=0$ to find $q$ and check with length powers.
walkthrough: Identify units: $[v] = \text{m s}^{-1}$, $[T] = \text{N} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$, $[\mu] = \text{kg m}^{-1}$.
Write homogeneity as $\text{m}^1 \text{s}^{-1} = (\text{kg m s}^{-2})^p (\text{kg m}^{-1})^q = \text{kg}^{p+q} \text{m}^{p-q} \text{s}^{-2p}$.
Equate powers of $\text{s}$: $-2p = -1$, so $p = 1/2$. This means wave speed increases with tension.
Equate powers of $\text{kg}$: $p+q = 0$, so $q = -p = -1/2$. This means wave speed decreases with mass per unit length.
Check powers of $\text{m}$: $p-q = 1/2 - (-1/2) = 1$, which matches $\text{m}^1$ on the left, confirming consistency.
Thus $v = T^{1/2} \mu^{-1/2} = \sqrt{T/\mu}$. This is option C.
